newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-"BUFFALO BILL" TOMBA APPEALS FOR CALM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-"BUFFALO BILL" TOMBA APPEALS FOR CALM.

text.p: Alberto Tomba, surprisingly cast as the "Buffalo Bill" of Alpine skiing, took his lead from Greta Garbo on Sunday.

The Italian, putting in a star appearance at the by now traditionally chaotic pre-world championship Tomba news conference, emerged from behind a barrage of cameras and television crews to appeal for solitude.

He also kept the world guessing about his future, saying that he would decide at the end of the season, and shrugged off Italian newspaper reports that he had pestered a Colombian starlet with repeated telephone messages.
Tomba, under more searching scrutiny in Italy than ever before, did not repeat Garbo's "I want to be alone" but the message to the media was unmistakable.
"I'll be going home tomorrow," said the triple Olympic gold medallist and double world champion, dressed casually in a checked jacket and blue polo neck.
"I ask you, if possible, to leave me in peace. Every two days I'll give you a report on how its going. I'll be alone. Just me and my staff...I don't want anybody else."

Winner of a floodlit slalom in Schladming, Austria, last Thursday week for the 48th World Cup victory of his career and his first as a 30-year-old, Tomba is the star attraction of the championships which open in Sestriere on Sunday.
He is the Italian flag-bearer at Sunday's opening ceremony but has 10 days before his first race.

Tomba almost retired last year after winning the slalom and giant world titles but said he stayed on because he wanted to race before his army of fans in a big event at home and at the resort where he won his first race in 1987.
He said skiing in Italy was both an advantage, because he knew the pistes and could count on huge support, and a disadvantage because of the pressure.

Giovanni Agnelli, whose grandfather and father founded Sestriere and whose family owns Juventus soccer club and controls the car giant Fiat, commented on Tomba in the family-owned La Stampa newspaper on Sunday.
"He's a showman as Buffalo Bill, in his time, must have been, the number one self-promoter," he said.
Asked whether he liked the comparison, Tomba gave every impression of not knowing who Buffalo Bill was.
Tiziana Nasi, president of the Sestriere organising committee and herself of the Agnelli family, said Buffalo Bill was "a nice person. It's a compliment."
Commenting on his form, "La Bomba" said he was primed and ready for his races on February 12 and 15.
He made no predictions about how Italy would fare but hoped his country would do as well as, if not better than, they did in Sierra Nevada when they captured four gold medals.
"I think that if 'Albertone' does not do it, there are a lot of others who will," Tomba declared.
Asked by a Japanese reporter whether he would be at the Nagano Olympics next year, the Italian replied jokingly: "As a journalist or as a competitor?"
He said later that he needed a world silver medal and an Olympic bronze to complete his collection and Sestriere and Nagano might be the places to pick them up.

"Nagano is a long way off," he added. "It's near in one sense though. It could be my fourth Olympics. it could be a great appointment to say enough...I have not made any plans yet. Give me a call me after the world championships."
Questions about other calls went down less well.
Newspapers had reported that Tomba had left several messages on the answerphone of Lorena Forteza, the star of a popular Italian film "Il Ciclone" (The Cyclone) last summer.
Tomba has said he had been asked to call her by someone associated with her and had been set up.
"People always want to invent something. Someone wants to publicise her a bit more...If she were famous, it would not have happened. I'm sorry. Its a nothing story."
